4. Finding the concept IDs you need

David Sarrat González

Source: vignettes/book-04-vocabulary.Rmd
book-04-vocabulary.Rmd

What you will learn

Find meanings, look up names and define a reusable concept set.

This chapter uses the public synthetic GiBleed practice connection from Getting started. You need: the packages and the matching practice connection described in Before you start. Run the sections in order in one R session. All printed results below were computed with dsOMOP and dsOMOPClient 2.10.5. They are teaching data, not clinical findings.

Start this chapter

Start a fresh R session in the book-work directory created in Getting started. Run this setup first:

library(dsOMOPClient)
source("tools/book/display.R")
source("tools/book/connection.R")
source("tools/book/practice.R")
practice <- if (book_driver == "DSLite") book_practice("gibleed") else book_connect("gibleed")
conns <- practice$conns
names(conns)
#> [1] "site"

The site connection is ready. The shared connection.R selects DSLite or Opal and resolves the resource names.

Search a name, then narrow the meaning

A concept is a public vocabulary meaning. Start broadly, then constrain the domain (kind of clinical fact), vocabulary (coding system) and standard status. Standard concepts are the preferred OMOP targets; classification concepts group them, and source concepts may map to them. None of this establishes patient use.

hits <- ds.omop.concept.search("Asthma", conns = conns)
knitr::kable(head(hits$pooled[c("concept_name", "domain_id", "vocabulary_id", "standard_concept")], 8))
concept_name domain_id vocabulary_id standard_concept
Childhood asthma Condition SNOMED S
Asthma Condition SNOMED S
Asthma screening Procedure SNOMED S

Now keep valid standard SNOMED conditions. The explicit filters make the search reproducible; a word alone can also match findings or history-of conditions.

conditions <- ds.omop.concept.search("Asthma", domain = "Condition",
  vocabulary = "SNOMED", standard_only = TRUE, valid = TRUE, conns = conns)
knitr::kable(head(conditions$pooled[c("concept_name", "concept_class_id")], 8))
concept_name concept_class_id
Childhood asthma Clinical Finding
Asthma Clinical Finding 
asthma_id <- conditions$pooled$concept_id[conditions$pooled$concept_name == "Asthma"]
stopifnot(length(asthma_id) == 1L)

Exercise 1 (basic). Broaden the query to non-standard concepts. Does that change the patient population yet?

Solution 1

broad <- ds.omop.concept.search("Asthma", standard_only = FALSE, conns = conns)
knitr::kable(head(broad$pooled[c("concept_name", "vocabulary_id", "standard_concept")], 8))
concept_name vocabulary_id standard_concept
Childhood asthma SNOMED S
Asthma SNOMED S
Asthma screening SNOMED S

No: this is a catalogue search. No clinical rows have been selected.

Read a concept and its mappings

lookup() returns the compact identity fields; the filtered search above also returns the full metadata used here. The concept class says what sort of vocabulary item this is. Valid dates delimit its vocabulary validity, not the dates of patient records. An invalid reason is about a vocabulary entry, not a patient’s diagnosis.

asthma_info <- ds.omop.concept.lookup(asthma_id, conns = conns)
knitr::kable(conditions$pooled[conditions$pooled$concept_id == asthma_id, c("concept_name", "standard_concept",
  "concept_class_id", "valid_start_date", "valid_end_date", "invalid_reason")])
concept_name standard_concept concept_class_id valid_start_date valid_end_date invalid_reason
2 Asthma S Clinical Finding 1970-01-01 2099-12-31 NA

A source code’s Maps to relationship can identify its standard target. Inspect the relationship direction and target before using mapped expansion. A standard concept may map to itself; that is not an additional diagnosis.

mappings <- ds.omop.concept.relationships(asthma_id,
  relationship_id = "Maps to", conns = conns)
print(data.frame(returned_relationships = NROW(mappings$pooled)))
#>   returned_relationships
#> 1                      0

An empty relationship result means this practice vocabulary has no returned mapping for the requested direction. It does not establish that all source codes are standard; inspect the source code itself in your own vocabulary.

Walk down and up the hierarchy

Descendants are more specific meanings. Ancestors are broader meanings. A SNOMED parent can have many clinically different children: inspect before pooling.

desc <- ds.omop.concept.descendants(asthma_id, include_self = FALSE, conns = conns)
knitr::kable(head(desc$pooled["concept_name"], 8))
concept_name
Childhood asthma 
parents <- ds.omop.concept.ancestors(asthma_id, conns = conns)
knitr::kable(head(parents$pooled["concept_name"], 8))
concept_name
Childhood asthma

For medicines, ATC is a classification vocabulary, so the default standard_only = TRUE can hide the class you need. This is a common pitfall.

atc <- ds.omop.concept.search(NULL, vocabulary = "ATC",
  standard_only = FALSE, conns = conns)
print(data.frame(returned_ATC_classes = NROW(atc$pooled)))
#>   returned_ATC_classes
#> 1                    0

If this subset vocabulary returns zero ATC classes, stop: no ATC-class study can be inferred from ingredient names. An authorised resource with that vocabulary is needed. Do not fabricate a class or silently substitute an ingredient.

Only use a returned class when its description matches the protocol. The drug utilisation case study below expands the selected class and inspects its members.

Check that the concept occurs here

Vocabulary presence is different from clinical prevalence. Prevalence is a protected aggregate over a table, with metric = "persons" by default. It has no concept_ids filter: select the row from the returned protected table. A concept outside the requested top list need not be absent.

prevalence <- ds.omop.concept.prevalence("condition_occurrence",
  metric = "persons", top_n = 20, scope = "pooled", conns = conns)
knitr::kable(prevalence$pooled)
concept_id n_persons concept_name
80180 2690 Osteoarthritis
40481087 2685 Viral sinusitis
4112343 2605 Acute viral pharyngitis
260139 2540 Acute bronchitis
372328 2025 Otitis media
28060 1675 Streptococcal sore throat
81151 1355 Sprain of ankle
378001 850 Concussion with no loss of consciousness
4283893 830 Sinusitis
257012 810 Chronic sinusitis
4027663 800 Peptic ulcer
4294548 785 Acute bacterial sinusitis
4218389 705 Whiplash injury to neck
78272 675 Sprain of wrist
4278672 510 Fracture of forearm
192671 475 Gastrointestinal hemorrhage
4113008 460 Laceration of hand
4152936 455 Laceration of thigh
4155034 455 Laceration of forearm
4156265 455 Facial laceration

Locate instead accepts concept IDs and reports which clinical columns use them. It is also protected: it is not a way to recover exact small cell counts.

locations <- ds.omop.concept.locate(asthma_id, scope = "pooled", conns = conns)
knitr::kable(locations$pooled)
concept_id table_name concept_column n_records n_persons
317009 condition_era condition_concept_id 5 5
317009 condition_occurrence condition_concept_id 5 5

Read a band as a band, a suppressed result as unavailable, and an absent top-list entry as inconclusive. Never replace those with zero in a study denominator.

Save the definition, including exclusions

Save the local definition rather than copying a transient list of search rows. This preserves whether descendants and mapped concepts belong in the set.

asthma <- omop_concept_set(asthma_id, descendants = TRUE)
asthma_exact <- omop_concept_set(asthma_id, descendants = FALSE)
class(asthma)
#> [1] "omop_concept_set" "list"

Exercise 2 (intermediate). Exclude the seed itself while keeping its children. Save the definition and read it back without accessing patients.

Solution 2

children_only <- omop_concept_set(asthma_id, descendants = TRUE,
  exclude = omop_concept_set(asthma_id, descendants = FALSE))
concept_file <- "book-concepts.rds"
saveRDS(list(asthma = asthma, children_only = children_only), concept_file)
saved_sets <- readRDS(concept_file)
identical(saved_sets$children_only, children_only)
#> [1] TRUE

The result is TRUE. An excluded set can itself use descendants when you intend to remove an entire subtree. Keep these definitions with the study protocol.

Find inpatient and outpatient visits

The setting is visit_concept_id; visit_type_concept_id describes provenance. The names below produce the IDs used in the visit chapters.

visit_hits <- ds.omop.concept.search("Visit", domain = "Visit", conns = conns)
visit_catalogue <- visit_hits$pooled[visit_hits$pooled$concept_name %in%
  c("Inpatient Visit", "Outpatient Visit"), ]
knitr::kable(visit_catalogue[c("concept_name", "standard_concept")])
concept_name standard_concept
Inpatient Visit S
Outpatient Visit S 
visit_ids <- setNames(visit_catalogue$concept_id, visit_catalogue$concept_name)
visit_sets <- lapply(visit_ids, omop_concept_set)
ds.omop.concept.locate(unname(visit_ids), scope = "pooled", conns = conns)$pooled
#>   concept_id       table_name   concept_column n_records n_persons
#> 1       9201 visit_occurrence visit_concept_id      1035       890

Find the colleague’s questions, answers and causes

The questionnaire fixture is explicitly synthetic and separate from GiBleed. Its local concepts are teaching examples, not codes to use in a real HDSS. Search the whole small catalogue so the question, answer and cause roles are visible together. Later questionnaire chapters refer back to this catalogue.

ds.omop.disconnect(conns = conns)
DSI::datashield.logout(conns)
source("tools/book/fixture.R")
practice <- book_fixture()
conns <- practice$conns
questionnaire <- ds.omop.concept.search(NULL, standard_only = FALSE,
  limit = 100, conns = conns)$pooled
knitr::kable(questionnaire[c("concept_name", "domain_id", "standard_concept")])
concept_name domain_id standard_concept
Education question Observation S
Fever question Observation S
Secondary education Meas Value S
University education Meas Value S
Myocardial infarction Condition S
Pneumonia Condition S
Yes Meas Value S
No Meas Value S
Inpatient Visit Meas Value S
Outpatient Visit Meas Value S
Education answer Meas Value S
Practice medicine Drug S
Practice measurement Measurement S
kilogram Unit S 
question_ids <- setNames(questionnaire$concept_id, questionnaire$concept_name)
education_set <- omop_concept_set(unname(question_ids["Education question"]))
cause_sets <- lapply(question_ids[c("Myocardial infarction", "Pneumonia")], omop_concept_set)

The education question selects observations. Secondary and University education are possible answers in value_as_concept_id. Myocardial infarction and Pneumonia are coded causes in death. Local fixture concepts have no external mapping or hierarchy; do not invent SNOMED or ATC ancestry for them.

question_presence <- ds.omop.concept.prevalence("observation", scope = "pooled", conns = conns)
knitr::kable(question_presence$pooled[setdiff(names(question_presence$pooled), "concept_id")])
n_persons concept_name
10 Education question
10 Fever question 
knitr::kable(ds.omop.concept.locate(unname(question_ids[c("Myocardial infarction", "Pneumonia")]),
  scope = "pooled", conns = conns)$pooled)
concept_id table_name concept_column n_records n_persons
900201 death cause_concept_id 10 10
900202 death cause_concept_id 5 5

Find haemoglobin, glucose and their units in Synthea

Switch to the numeric resource. The vocabulary spells haemoglobin “Hemoglobin”. Select the precise test and specimen, not every hit containing the word.

ds.omop.disconnect(conns = conns)
DSI::datashield.logout(conns)
unlink(practice$path)
practice <- book_connect("numeric")
conns <- practice$conns
lab_hits <- ds.omop.concept.search("Hemoglobin", domain = "Measurement", conns = conns)$pooled
knitr::kable(lab_hits[c("concept_name", "vocabulary_id", "standard_concept")])
concept_name vocabulary_id standard_concept
Hemoglobin and Hematocrit panel - Blood LOINC S
Hemoglobin A1c/Hemoglobin.total in Blood LOINC S
Hemoglobin.gastrointestinal.lower [Presence] in Stool by Immunoassay –1st specimen LOINC S
Hemoglobin [Presence] in Urine by Test strip LOINC S
Hemoglobin [Mass/volume] in Blood LOINC S 
hb_id <- lab_hits$concept_id[lab_hits$concept_name == "Hemoglobin [Mass/volume] in Blood"]
glucose_hits <- ds.omop.concept.search("Glucose", domain = "Measurement", conns = conns)$pooled
knitr::kable(glucose_hits[c("concept_name", "vocabulary_id", "standard_concept")])
concept_name vocabulary_id standard_concept
Glucose tolerance test SNOMED S
Urine screening for glucose SNOMED S
Self-monitoring of blood glucose SNOMED S
Glucose [Mass/volume] in Blood LOINC S
Glucose [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma LOINC S
Glucose [Presence] in Urine by Test strip LOINC S
Glucose [Mass/volume] in Urine by Test strip LOINC S 
lab_sets <- list(haemoglobin = omop_concept_set(hb_id),
  glucose = omop_concept_set(glucose_hits$concept_id))

These glucose hits are a catalogue, not yet an interchangeable measurement set. The chronic-disease study selects a single specimen and concentration measure.

units <- ds.omop.value.counts("measurement", "unit_concept_id", concept_id = hb_id,
  scope = "pooled", conns = conns)
knitr::kable(units$pooled)
n concept_name value
105 gram per deciliter 8713

Counts describe recorded unit use under disclosure control. A vocabulary lookup of “milligram per deciliter” alone cannot establish that the lab was stored that way.

Exercise 3 (advanced). Check glucose unit use and save its catalogue together with the haemoglobin set. Why is choosing all glucose hits premature?

Solution 3

glucose_units <- ds.omop.value.counts("measurement", "unit_concept_id",
  concept_id = glucose_hits$concept_id[glucose_hits$concept_name == "Glucose [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma"], scope = "pooled", conns = conns)
knitr::kable(glucose_units$pooled)
saveRDS(list(sets = lab_sets, glucose_catalogue = glucose_hits,
  visit_sets = visit_sets, education = education_set, causes = cause_sets,
  questionnaire_catalogue = questionnaire), concept_file)
identical(readRDS(concept_file)$sets, lab_sets)
#> [1] TRUE

Keep book-concepts.rds with your study files. In a later session, readRDS("book-concepts.rds")$education reuses the saved education definition; the questionnaire catalogue records the IDs used in subsequent examples.

Different specimens, mass versus molar concentrations and urine versus blood measurements need different definitions. Preserve that decision with the set.

Recap

Search, inspect standard status and mappings, explore ancestry, check protected clinical use, then save the definition. The subsequent chapters reuse these catalogues; the case studies repeat the same process for their research question.
